Hannah / team —

Quick read-through after the attachments — high-level technical points below. I ran the sample p95 tokenized request traces against the Cloudflare and Fastly perf sheets the vendors provided (back-of-envelope). Akamai's SOW has fewer performance metrics, asked them to send latency histograms.

Highlights:
- Performance: Cloudflare shows best p95 origin->edge latency in NA for our request mix (small JSON APIs) in their profile. Fastly is close but shows higher variance at peak.
- Caching: Fastly's edge keying gives us the most control for our prefix caching strategy. Cloudflare's managed caching is simpler but less flexible for custom keying rules; may reduce hit rate for some of our microservices.
- WAF: Cloudflare's ruleset has more managed detection for supply-chain vulnerabilities (good), Akamai's solution appears strongest for bot mitigation.
- Operational risk: consolidating to Cloudflare reduces cross-vendor operational overhead (one ACLs/signed tokens), but increases dependency. If we consolidate, we should negotiate portability clauses and exportable cache metadata.
- Integration work: switching full traffic would require ~4 weeks of staging, plus a rollback plan.

Recommendation (tech): Prefer Cloudflare if the commercial is within ~15% of Fastly. If Fastly is materially cheaper (>=25% delta) we should consider splitting gateway (Fastly edge + Cloudflare WAF overlay) to retain cache control while using CF for WAF.

I'll follow up with more detailed request patterns Monday.

-- Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infra | Redwood Inference

Team —

Security notes on the three proposals (high level):
- Cloudflare: SOC 2 Type II report available; offers SOC2 + ISO27001. Strong managed WAF rules and rapid ruleset updates. Need to confirm logging retention and whether logs for redwood requests can be routed to our S3 in us-west-2 with encryption-at-rest and separate KMS. Contract items to require: breach notification <=72 hours, right to audit (annual), and by-default TLS 1.3 for all edge-communications.
- Fastly: SOC2 available; edge-control is attractive but their WAF is modular (Signal Sciences) — ask for managed tuning SLA. Also check E-Tag handling and cache-control header guidance to avoid accidental sensitive-data caching.
- Akamai: good bot mitigation and edge ACL features; contract has typical language that pushes liability; be ready to push for clearer incident LTTR and indemnity carve-outs.

If we consolidate, insist on:
1) Data export portability clause (cache keys + routing metadata)
2) Logging export streams to our account (no vendor-owned bucket)
3) Security addendum referencing SOC2 attestation and incident timelines

I'll draft a short addendum text for Jordan to weave into the negotiation.

Laura Bennett
CISO | Redwood Inference
